question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹1,200 at an interest rate of 4% per month for 12 months.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the rate is given per month and time is given in months, we can directly apply the simple interest formula without converting units.

SI = (Principal × Rate × Time) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (1200 × 4 × 12) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 12 × 48 = 576

**∴ The correct answer is ₹576.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1200

Rate of Interest (R) = 4% per month

Time (T) = 12 months

 
 P = ₹1200
 
 
• 
 

 
 R = 4% per month
 T = 12 months
 
 
 SI = ₹576

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI = (1200 × 4 × 12) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 12 × 4 × 12

⇒ SI = 12 × 48

⇒ SI = 576

**∴ The correct answer is ₹576.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount (A)

The total amount at the end of the specified term is the sum of the principal and the accrued interest. The formula is A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Time & Rate Consistency

Always ensure that the unit of Time (T) matches the frequency of the Interest Rate (R). If the rate is per month, the time must be in months. If the rate is per annum, the time must be in years.

Compound Interest (CI)

Unlike Simple Interest, Compound Interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest from previous periods. The formula used is A = P(1 + R/100)T.
